summary: Dedicated pool throughput lull from prefetch-shadowing and gang-preemption during mixed short/long stream workload
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightQuant reported recurring midday throughput degradation in their eu-west dedicated pool over last 36 hours. Symptoms: p50 stable, p95/p99 inflating by 2-4x for short text-generation routes and a corresponding drop in sustained batch throughput. Impact: customer reports missed SLAs for latency-sensitive endpoints and falling behind ingestion windows.

Impact:
- Multiple customer routes (low-latency chat) see p95 from ~200ms to ~1s during 11:30-13:45 UTC windows.
- Batch pipelines (scheduled hourly) experience enqueue growth and 30-40% throughput drop while autoscaler remains stable (no scale events).
- Customer-facing errors: rare 5xx spikes (~0.3% of requests) tied to timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id d-pool-eu-09 assigned to BrightQuant (reserved capacity).
- Models serving: redwood/decoder-7B-v2 pinned.
- Traffic mix: many long-lived, low-CPU streams (analytics listeners) + short high-QPS chatlets.
- Observed on infra: prod eu-west; telemetry retained in Redwood Console (dash links below).

Steps to reproduce / Observed triggers:
1) In customer traffic during mid-day, dozens of long-lived connections with intermittent token generation overlap with a scheduled hourly batch of 128-sequence inference jobs.
2) Prefetch subsystem initiates KV warmup for long contexts; prefetch tasks consume HBM bandwidth and PCIe IO windows.
3) When batch sweep starts, scheduler attempts gang-attach for batch jobs; GPU handshake latencies spike (nvlink/PCIe handshakes delayed) causing serialized attach and temporary slot blocking.
4) Autoscaler metrics (slot utilization) remain within thresholds, so no immediate scale action; result is temporary queueing and degraded per-request latencies.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Console dashboard: /org/brightquant/dedicated/pool/d-pool-eu-09/perf (p95/p99 charts)
- Trace: trace-id 4f3a2b6c (example of serialized attach and prefetch overlap)
- Slack: #support (thread tD3kz9)

Initial hypotheses:
- Prefetch jobs (long-lived stream KV growth) are interfering with batch attach handshake windows (HBM + PCIe contention).
- Scheduler gang-preemption policy delayed eviction of long-lived streams, producing a blocking window where batch workloads are forced to serialize.
- Autoscaler sensor does not capture transient HBM/handshake latency, so it fails to scale preemptively.
investigation:
Timeline & findings:
- 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: BrightQuant reported first spike; Support created initial ticket and collected traces.
- 2026-03-12 12:15 UTC: SRE replicated with internal load generator combining 200 long-lived streams + scheduled batch; reproduced p99 spike and observed repeated GPU attach handshakes in node logs.
- 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC: Kernel-level NVLINK counters show short bursts of PCIe tx retries during batch attach (~30-80ms windows).
- 2026-03-13 09:20 UTC: Prefetch worker metrics show sustained KV cache churn and HBM bandwidth at 78-92% during window.
- 2026-03-14 06:40 UTC: Investigated autoscaler telemetry; slot-util metrics do not reflect handshake tail latency - autoscaler thresholds insufficient for this mixed-workload pattern.

Collected artifacts:
- node logs: /var/log/redwood/node-attach-2026-03-12-12.log (excerpt attached in ticket)
- sample traces: trace 4f3a2b6c, 66b1d1f2
- perf counters snapshot: /s3/redwood-debug/prefetch-hbm-snap-2026-03-13.json

Intermediate conclusion:
- Root cause likely multi-factor: prefetch-driven HBM pressure + serialized GPU attach (gang-scheduler behavior) causing temporary slot blocking; autoscaler blind spot for handshake latency allows the condition to persist for 60-180s windows.
resolution:
Mitigation steps applied (temporary):
1) Disabled aggressive prefetch for BrightQuant pool during peak window via runtime flag (prefetch.max_concurrent -> 4). This reduced HBM pressure and eliminated attach serialization in test.
2) Updated gang-scheduler soft-eviction threshold to prefer preempting the oldest long-lived streams when a batch attach is pending for >500ms (hotfix rollout to eu-west pool).
3) Added autoscaler sensor patch to monitor GPU attach latency metric (attach_handshake_ms) and treat sustained >200ms as a scale trigger. Patch deployed as canary to two dedicated pools.

Planned follow-ups:
- Engineering to land comprehensive fix: improved prefetch backpressure + smarter gang-attach backoff (PR linked). Target sprint: 2026-03-21.
- Postmortem runbook update: document prefetch throttles for dedicated pools and standard mitigation steps.
- Customer follow-up: confirm SLA recovery and offer temporary additional capacity credit for impacted windows.

Status: ongoing. Mitigations reduced p99 by ~60% in canary and prevented queueing; monitoring continues.
